blocks.text: 1. Recursive RAG
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721033-249078496.png

Agentic RAG closed out the Advanced RAG module, previewing an agent freely choosing between tools. Recursive RAG, where retrieval repeatedly refines its own results, opens the final stretch of this module with a narrower, more structured form of repetition.
It feeds each retrieval round's output back in as input to the next round, a refine and repeat technique explored in full throughout this topic.
2. One Pass Versus Repeated Refinement
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721256-414445182.png
Naive RAG retrieves once, in a single pass, and accepts whatever it finds.
Recursive RAG instead retrieves, evaluates, and retrieves again using what it just learned.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","How many retrieval rounds"],"rows":[["Naive RAG","Exactly one retrieval round"],["Recursive RAG","Several rounds, each informed by the last"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Each Round Narrows The Answer
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721257-413521079.png
The first retrieval round surfaces broad, general context.
Each following round uses that context to retrieve more specific, targeted chunks.
4. A Termination Condition Is Required
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721257-494396864.png
Much like the runaway loops covered in Agentic RAG, without a defined stopping point, recursion can continue past the point of adding value.
A maximum round count or a diminishing returns check keeps it bounded.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A recursive pipeline with no round limit at all risks the same unbounded looping covered generally in agentic loops, just in a narrower, retrieval-specific form.

blocks.text: 5. Recursive Decomposition Of The Query
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721258-868167826.png
Much like the multi-hop questions covered in Chain Of Thought, a complex question can be broken into a smaller sub-question at each recursive round.
Each sub-question's answer feeds into solving the next one.
6. Recursive RAG Versus Multi-Step Agentic Loops
Unlike the free per-step planning covered in Agentic RAG, recursive RAG follows one fixed refine and repeat pattern, while an agent chooses freely between different tools at each step.
This makes it a narrower, more predictable form of repeated retrieval.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Pattern","Predictability"],"rows":[["Recursive RAG","Fixed refine and repeat pattern, predictable"],["Agentic loop","Free tool choice per step, less predictable"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Diminishing Returns Across Rounds
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721258-392667862.png
Each additional recursive round typically adds less new useful information than the round before it.
This makes a small, fixed round limit usually sufficient in practice.
8. Cost Grows With Each Round
As Advanced RAG covers, each added step costs latency, and every recursive round is its own retrieval and generation call.
This directly multiplies latency and cost by the number of rounds run.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running three recursive rounds means three separate retrieval and generation calls, a real multiplier on cost that the diminishing returns of later rounds must justify.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Recursive RAG Earns Its Per-Round Cost

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Recursive RAG Earns Its Per-Round Cost
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721258-705537922.png
Broad questions needing progressive narrowing benefit from recursion.
A question already answerable in one retrieval pass, by contrast, does not need repeated rounds.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Running recursive retrieval with no termination condition or round limit at all.
Continuing rounds past the point where new context stops adding useful information.
Confusing recursive RAG's fixed refine and repeat pattern with free agentic tool choice.
Applying multiple recursive rounds to a question already answerable in one retrieval pass.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Recursive RAG feeds each retrieval round's output back in as input to the next round.
Naive RAG retrieves once; recursive RAG retrieves, evaluates, and retrieves again.
The first round surfaces broad context; later rounds retrieve more specific, targeted chunks.
A maximum round count or diminishing returns check is required to bound the recursion.
A complex question can be decomposed into a sub-question answered at each recursive round.
Recursive RAG follows one fixed pattern, unlike an agent's free per-step tool choice.
Each additional round typically adds less new useful information than the round before it.
Every recursive round is its own retrieval and generation call, multiplying cost by round count.
